task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: shot mix (distance and type) change after offensive substitutions
methodological_questions: Does changing the offensive five move shot mix relative to stints with an unchanged five?
Can the design separate personnel effects from shooter selection, game state, and opponent matchup?
Do placebo contrasts (other shot types, non-personnel changes) fail to show the same shift?
Do derived play-type or graph-derived labels leak outcome information into the shot-mix measure?
What sample and exposure are needed in each season and in playoffs?

historical_evidence.finding: PULL_UP exposure-effect diagnostics. With lineup fixed effects the slope holding shot fixed was -0.0255 (SE 0.0061). Without lineup FE it was -0.0063 (SE 0.0036), and the placebo on other play types was -0.0075 (SE 0.0017). [prior work] reads the shrinkage and placebo pattern as shooter-level confounding. Sample and power were not recorded.

Tail and null-model audit of a published suppression excess. Reproduced excess was 0.4080 (CI 0.378 to 0.438). Within-unit permutation residual was +0.0054 (z 0.40). Asymmetry test gave p 0.258 and drift-centred tail-mass ratio was 1.007. [prior work] attributes the apparent excess to construction, drift, exposure, and regression to the mean.

Double-suppression stacking (POST_UP then PUTBACK). Baseline 1.210 (n=960,764). Stacked 1.138 (d=-0.071, n=1,047) against an additive prediction of -0.232. The transition-cluster gradient was +0.075, against a hypothesised flat pattern. Limits recorded as implementation bug and small sample. Failure mechanism recorded as none.

Penalty-state adaptation (Pilot A). Penalty contrast any_fta 3->4 was -0.151, against placebo contrasts of -5.556 and -9.655. Rim_pct contrast was +0.015 against placebos of +1.666 and +2.077. Standard errors were not printed because of a sqrt warning. Sample and power were not recorded. Verdict recorded as null, failure type E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing a within-shooter exposure slope to defensive adaptation without controlling for lineup and shooter composition
failed_approaches.why: The effect shrank from -0.0255 to -0.0063 when lineup FE were removed, and the same-shooter placebo on other play types was of similar size. [prior work] judged this consistent with a shooter-level confound.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Excess of trigger drop over matched-control drop as evidence of an effect beyond null models
failed_approaches.why: Permutation residual was near zero (z 0.40), asymmetry was not significant, and the tail ratio was 1.007 after drift centring. Recorded limits were drift, insufficient exposure, selection, and regression to the mean.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing additive stacking of two opponent events against the next possession
failed_approaches.why: Stacked n was 1,047, and [prior work] flags a possible implementation bug and small sample. The result did not match the additive prediction (-0.071 against -0.232), and the transition gradient ran opposite to the hypothesis.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Penalty-state contrast with clock and game-by-period fixed effects
failed_approaches.why: The penalty contrast was not distinct from the placebo contrasts, standard errors were not printed, and power was not recorded (failure type E_unclear).

evidence_establishes: Earlier studies by this project in the retrieved set used placebo contrasts and null-model audits, and found that apparent effects in this family of play-level designs often shrank or failed when lineup, shooter, drift, or exposure were controlled.
Lineup and shooter fixed effects were needed to separate apparent effects from confounding in the one retrieved record that tested them directly ([prior work][prior work]).
Small-n contrasts and unprinted standard errors produced inconclusive results (FAM:[prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record studies offensive five changes or shot-mix composition (distance, type, attempts) as an outcome. None of the four records concerns offensive personnel.
No retrieved record reports a power analysis or minimum exposure for lineup-level shot-mix contrasts.
Nothing shows whether the 2022-23 to 2024-25 play-by-play, substitution intervals, or graph-derived play-type records are fit for this question.
The retrieved records do not show that the design can detect personnel effects; the question's premise is unverified.
own_inferences: Shot mix is partly determined by which positions are on the floor (for example, a big-heavy five takes more rim shots). A positive shot-mix shift after a personnel change may therefore be close to mechanical and says little about a causal lineup effect unless the design isolates it.
Framing the question as 'showing the design can detect personnel effects' presupposes a positive result. A validation test should be specified with pre-stated criteria for failure as well as success.
The shooter-level confound in [prior work][prior work] suggests shooter fixed effects are needed here too, because a lineup change often coincides with a change of shooter.
Playoff samples are probably too small for lineup-level shot-mix contrasts, so playoffs are best treated as a holdout or robustness check.
uncertainties: Retrieved records are from other study families (defensive suppression, penalty states, pull-up exposure) and may not transfer to offensive lineup shot mix.
Stint-level exposure counts for lineup changes in the stated data are unknown.
Whether the derived play-type records encode shot outcomes (and so leak into shot-mix labels) is not stated.
Season-level drift in the NBA shot profile over 2022-23 to 2024-25 is not quantified in the retrieved evidence.
Whether the substitution intervals capture within-possession changes or only between-possession ones is not confirmed.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records do not test offensive personnel, so they do not establish that the question is already answered or testable. They do show a recurring failure pattern in this project's play-level designs: shooter and lineup confounding ([prior work][prior work]), drift and regression to the mean ([prior work][prior work]), and underpowered or unverified contrasts (FAM:[prior work], [prior work][prior work]). That pattern moved the decision from an unconditional proceed to proceed_with_changes, with mandatory lineup and shooter controls, drift handling, a placebo design fixed in advance, and an explicit power check before any result is read.

blocking_constraints.text: Lineup change is confounded with shooter identity, game state, and opponent matchup. Without shooter and game-state controls the estimate can reflect selection rather than personnel.
Shot distance and type are partly determined by player positions, so a shot-mix shift may be near-mechanical and does not by itself show a causal personnel effect.
Playoff samples and rare five-man changes may give too few stints for stable shot-mix contrasts. Playoffs are likely underpowered.

prior_work.summary: None of the retrieved records tests offensive lineup changes or shot-mix composition. They address related designs: a shooter-level exposure slope (artifact), a null-model audit of a suppression excess (artifact), double-suppression stacking (inconclusive), and penalty-state adaptation (inconclusive). They are relevant as cautionary precedent on confounding, placebo dependence, drift, and power, not as an answer to the question.

risks.text: Shooter, game state, and opponent matchup may drive both the personnel change and the shot mix. [prior work][prior work] showed a shrinkage from -0.0255 to -0.0063 when lineup FE were removed.
Placebo contrasts may be as large as the effect ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]). The placebo must be fixed in advance and tested for separation from the effect.
Shot-distance mix follows from positions on the floor, so a shift may be mechanical and not a causal personnel effect.
Power was not recorded in the retrieved records ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]), and FAM:[prior work] was small-sample limited. Stint counts must be checked before analysis.
Playoff and rare-lineup-change cells may be too sparse for stable contrasts, as in [prior work][prior work].
Shot profiles and pace change across 2022-23 to 2024-25. [prior work][prior work] needed drift centring, so season and time effects are required.
Coaches substitute on game state and fatigue, and [prior work][prior work] found selection and regression to the mean. Substitution timing should be modelled, not assumed random.
Graph-derived play-type labels built from the play-by-play may encode shot outcome or points, so the shot-mix label may not be independent of the outcome.
FAM:[prior work] recorded a possible implementation bug. Stint assignment, clock joins, and possession boundaries should be validated on a sample before analysis.
Several shot-mix measures, lineup definitions, and placebos invite multiple comparisons. The primary estimand and correction must be fixed in advance.

design.estimand: Within-game change in offensive shot mix (share of rim attempts, share of 3PA, mean shot distance, shot-type share) when the offensive five changes by at least one player, compared with stints where the five is unchanged. Shooter and game-state controls are included. Evidence that the design can detect personnel effects is a validation criterion, not a premise.
design.unit: Offensive possession nested in a stint (continuous five-man interval). Shot attempts are the outcome unit, with shooter and possession as clusters.
design.sample: NBA regular season 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, with playoffs held out as a robustness check. Include only stints with at least a pre-specified minimum number of shot attempts. Exclude garbage time and fouls-to-give periods.
design.power: Before analysis, compute stint-level counts of five-man changes and shot attempts per team-season. Report the minimum detectable shot-mix shift at 80% power using a clustered design (teams, games, shooters). Abort the primary test if power is below target, and report the result as untestable at useful power rather than null.
design.controls: Game, team, and season fixed effects; game-by-period fixed effects; score margin and clock bins; opponent defensive five or matchup where available; shooter fixed effects in a specification with and without lineup FE, as in [prior work][prior work]; drift terms by season; substitution-timing controls for fatigue and game state (instrumented or modelled, not assumed random). Derived play-type labels are used only if independent of the outcome, and a sensitivity analysis is run without them.
design.falsification: Pre-register placebo contrasts: (a) shot-mix change at substitutions that do not alter the offensive five (for example, a same-five reorder); (b) shot-mix change in the defensive five, which should not move offensive shot mix; (c) shot-mix change in the 2022-23 season with 2024-25 placebo shifts. The positive finding fails if placebo contrasts are of comparable size to the effect (as in [prior work][prior work]) or if the effect vanishes when shooter FE are added.
design.multiplicity: Fix one primary estimand (rim-attempt share change after a five change) and one primary specification. Other shot-mix measures and placebos are secondary, with Holm or FDR correction across families.
design.decision_rule: Declare the design validated only if (1) power is adequate, (2) the primary effect is positive with a CI excluding zero after shooter and game-state controls, (3) placebo contrasts are null and separated from the effect, and (4) the effect holds in at least two of three seasons after drift terms. Report artifact if the effect shrinks materially under shooter or lineup FE or matches placebos. Report inconclusive if power or placebo separation fails. Do not report supported on the premise alone.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, as available on 2026-11-02. Play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes, box-score summary, and derived play-type records from [source] database. Record file versions and build dates before analysis.
